National Digital Fellowship 2026

Empowering early-career engineers, designers, and policy innovators to build scalable digital public infrastructure for 1.4 billion citizens.

Program Overview

The National Digital Fellowship is a prestigious 12-month full-time immersion program that embeds top technologists within central and state government ministries. Fellows work alongside senior civil servants and open-source architects to deploy production-grade civic tech platforms.

Over the past four cohorts, 120 fellows have authored core protocols, launched national registries, and improved service delivery across digital health, financial inclusion, and rural governance.

Specialization Tracks

Track 1: Public Health Technology

Architecting unified health interfaces, distributed health record repositories, and district-level disease surveillance systems.

Track 2: Open Financial Networks

Building next-generation open credit enablement networks, cross-border remittance gateways, and account aggregator frameworks.

Track 3: Agritech & Rural Logistics

Deploying digital crop survey registries, localized weather advisory integrations, and decentralized farmer marketplace protocols.

Track 4: Climate & Clean Energy Tech

Developing open grid telemetry platforms, carbon credit registries, and decentralized distributed energy management systems.

Eligibility & Fellowship Benefits

We welcome applications from passionate builders with 0 to 4 years of work experience across software engineering, UX research, data engineering, and technology law.

  • Stipend: A competitive monthly stipend of ₹75,000 (tax-exempt).
  • Duration: 12 months full-time starting January 15, 2027.
  • Location: Hybrid with central postings in New Delhi, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.
  • Healthcare: Comprehensive medical insurance coverage of ₹5,00,000 for fellows and dependents.
  • Travel: Relocation allowance of ₹25,000 plus domestic travel reimbursements for field deployments.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible to apply for the fellowship?
Applicants must hold a recognized bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, design, economics, or public policy by December 2026, with between 0 and 4 years of professional experience.
What is the duration and location of the fellowship?
The program runs for exactly 12 months, from January 2027 through December 2027. Fellows spend the first 4 weeks in intensive residency in New Delhi before joining their ministry partner teams.
What is the monthly stipend and financial support?
All selected fellows receive a monthly living stipend of ₹75,000. In addition, health insurance of ₹5,00,000 and a relocation allowance of ₹25,000 are provided.
How does the selection process work?
The selection process comprises three stages: an online application with technical portfolio review, an asynchronous take-home system design case study, and a final panel interview with ministry stakeholders.
Fellows choose among four specialized domains: Public Health Technology, Open Financial Networks, Agritech & Rural Logistics, and Climate & Clean Energy Tech.
No prior government experience is necessary. We seek mission-driven builders with strong technical craft, problem-solving mindset, and passion for civic impact.
Yes, final-year undergraduate and graduate students graduating by December 2026 are fully eligible to apply, provided they can join full-time by January 15, 2027.
Alumni frequently transition to full-time roles in digital public infrastructure bodies, venture-backed civic tech startups, philanthropic foundations, or top-tier international policy labs.
Applicants must submit an updated resume (PDF), links to GitHub repositories or design portfolios, and two short written essays addressing digital infrastructure challenges.
